## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: every cent rounding (line net and VAT) now goes through a new `_round_cent` helper, which rounds half-up explicitly (`ROUND_HALF_UP`).
- `tests/test_totals.py`: I added tests for half-cent ties in VAT and in line nets, plus one test that results don't depend on the ambient decimal context.

- **`line_net`:** it had the same flaw for fractional quantities and prices. For example, 0.5 x 0.05 = 0.025 became 0.02 instead of 0.03.

## Verification

So VAT is still computed once on the subtotal. Finance can settle this by looking up an invoice with three lines of 1 x 0.25 at 10% in Ledgerline. I also haven't checked credit notes. Half-up here rounds ties away from zero (-0.125 becomes -0.13), and I don't know how Ledgerline handles negatives.

# Notes: invoice totals now use Ledgerline's rounding (half-up)

The INV-2291 test now passes (1.38) and the suite is 6 passed. I fixed the rounding mode, which is documented and verified. I did not switch VAT to per-line, which a findings-mirror entry recommends but I couldn't confirm. That is the one open question below.

## What changed
- `invoicing/totals.py`: all rounding to the cent is now explicit half-up (`ROUND_HALF_UP`), through one helper, `to_cent()`. It is used for both the line net and the VAT.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: three new tests (VAT 0.025 -> 0.03; line net 0.525 -> 0.53; the result does not depend on the caller's decimal context).
- `python3 -m pytest -q`: 6 passed, including INV-2291. INV-2291 and the three new tests fail against the old code.
- The implementation also matches an independent half-up reference on 200,000 random invoices.

## Why
`Decimal.quantize(CENT)` with no `rounding=` argument uses the decimal context default, which is half-even (banker's rounding). For INV-2291 the VAT is 1.25 x 0.10 = 0.125. That became 0.12 (total 1.37). Half-up gives 0.13 (total 1.38), which is what Ledgerline has. `docs/accounting-rules.md` rule 2 already says rounding is half-up, so the code was out of line with our own rules. Line net had the same flaw and is fixed too. On simulated random invoices this changes about 2-3% of totals, which fits "sometimes off by one cent".

## Open question, not changed: per-line VAT
The findings mirror has one relevant entry (6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, gpt-5, 2026-09-14). It agrees on half-up. It also claims that Ledgerline computes VAT per line (round each line's VAT half-up, then sum) rather than once on the subtotal. I did not adopt that part:
- Nothing in this repo supports it and our rules doc is silent on it. The entry comes from another team's setup (Ledgerline API v3), and I could not check it against our Ledgerline.
- INV-2291 and every test give the same answer either way, so our evidence cannot tell the two methods apart.
- The methods differ a lot. On simulated invoices they disagree on 0% of single-line, about 21% of 2-line, 31% of 3-line and 44% of 5-line invoices. Switching on a guess could break many invoices that match today.

To settle it, take an invoice with two 0.25 lines at 10% VAT. A Ledgerline total of 0.55 means VAT on the subtotal (what the code does now). 0.56 means per-line VAT. Finance's mismatch rate on multi-line invoices before this fix is also a hint: about 2% fits the rounding bug alone, while 20% or more would point to per-line VAT. If it is per-line, the change is small: compute `to_cent(line_net * rate)` for each line in `invoice_totals` and sum those.

# Fix: invoice totals one cent off from Ledgerline

All 5 tests pass now (before: 2 passed, 1 failed). The failing INV-2291 test is fixed. One open question about how Ledgerline computes VAT is below, and I did not change that behavior.

## Cause
`invoicing/totals.py` rounded with `Decimal.quantize(CENT)` and no rounding argument. That uses the decimal context default, ROUND_HALF_EVEN. `docs/accounting-rules.md` (rule 2) says Ledgerline rounds half-up. The two only differ on exact ties. For INV-2291 the VAT is 1.25 x 0.10 = 0.125. We rounded it to 0.12 (total 1.37). Ledgerline rounds it to 0.13 (total 1.38).

## Change
- `invoicing/totals.py`: added `_round_cent()` (ROUND_HALF_UP) and used it for both roundings, line net and VAT. VAT is still computed once on the invoice subtotal, as before.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added two regression tests, one for a VAT tie (1.25 at 10% gives VAT 0.13) and one for a line-net tie (1.5 x 0.15 gives 0.23). Both use a single line on purpose, so they hold whether or not Ledgerline rounds VAT per line. I checked that both fail on the old rounding.
- `NOTES.md`: written in the project root with this same summary.

## Open question I did not change: per-line VAT
The findings mirror had one relevant note (id 6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, author unknown). It claims Ledgerline computes VAT per line and sums the rounded amounts, and that fixing the rounding mode alone is not enough. Its half-even point matches what I found, but I did not adopt the per-line part:
- INV-2291 cannot tell the two methods apart. With half-up rounding, VAT on the subtotal and per-line VAT both give 0.13 and a total of 1.38.
- Nothing in this repo supports per-line VAT (the docs don't mention it), and I can't query Ledgerline from here.
- Switching would change VAT on every multi-line invoice, not just ties, and can move it by more than a cent. Four lines of 0.15 at 10% give VAT 0.06 on the subtotal and 0.08 per line. If Ledgerline works on the subtotal, the switch would break invoices that match today.

To settle it, finance can take a real multi-line invoice from Ledgerline where the methods differ and compare VAT. For example, two lines of 0.25 at 10% give VAT 0.05 on the subtotal and 0.06 per line. If Ledgerline shows the per-line figure, per-line VAT is a small follow-up change in `invoice_totals`.

Also unverified: ties on negative amounts (credit notes) round away from zero, which is what Python's ROUND_HALF_UP does. The docs don't say how Ledgerline treats negative ties.

# Notes: invoice totals one cent off from Ledgerline (INV-2291)

The INV-2291 test now passes (all 4 tests pass), and INV-2291 totals 1.38. I deliberately did not take one claim from the findings archive, per-line VAT, because I couldn't verify it. That is an open question for finance (see the end).

## Cause

`Decimal.quantize(CENT)` with no rounding argument uses the decimal context default, ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding). Our rules (`docs/accounting-rules.md`, rule 2) say Ledgerline rounds half-up. The two only differ on exact half-cent amounts. INV-2291's VAT is exactly 0.125. We rounded it to 0.12, while Ledgerline's 1.38 implies 0.13, so we showed 1.37. `line_net` had the same flaw.

## Change

- `invoicing/totals.py`: new `round_cent()` that quantizes with an explicit `ROUND_HALF_UP`, used for both the line net and the VAT. VAT is still computed once on the invoice subtotal, as before.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added `test_line_net_rounds_half_up` for the line-net rounding site (0.5 x 0.25 = 0.125 -> 0.13).
- I compared old and new code on about 5,000 generated two-line invoices. Results differ only where a rounding step hits an exact half-cent tie, and nothing else changes.

## Open question: per-line VAT (deliberately not changed)

The only relevant entry in the findings mirror (`6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412`, author unknown) says Ledgerline also computes VAT per line and sums the rounded line amounts. I took its half-up point, since our own docs and the failing test back it. I did not take the per-line claim:

- INV-2291 gives 1.38 under both methods, so the failing test cannot tell them apart.
- Our docs do not mention per-line VAT, and nothing in this repo can confirm the claim.
- Switching changes VAT on many multi-line invoices. If the claim is wrong, we would create new one-cent mismatches.

To settle it, ask finance for Ledgerline's total on an invoice like one of these (10% VAT):

| Invoice | VAT on subtotal (current code) | VAT per line (archive claim) |
|---|---|---|
| 3 lines of 1 x 0.04 | VAT 0.01, total 0.13 | VAT 0.00, total 0.12 |
| 2 lines of 1 x 0.25 | VAT 0.05, total 0.55 | VAT 0.06, total 0.56 |

If Ledgerline matches the per-line column, `invoice_totals` should sum `round_cent(line_net * rate)` over the lines instead of rounding VAT once on the subtotal.

# INV-2291: one-cent mismatch with Ledgerline

## Cause
`invoicing/totals.py` rounded with `Decimal.quantize(CENT)` and no rounding mode, so it used the decimal default, ROUND_HALF_EVEN. `docs/accounting-rules.md` (rule 2) says rounding is half-up. INV-2291 has VAT of 1.25 x 0.10 = 0.125 exactly: half-even gives 0.12 (total 1.37), half-up gives 0.13 (total 1.38, Ledgerline's figure).

## Change
- `invoicing/totals.py`: new `round_to_cent()` quantizes with an explicit `ROUND_HALF_UP`. Both roundings (line net and VAT) use it. Public API unchanged.
- `tests/test_totals.py`: added `test_vat_rounds_half_up` and `test_line_net_rounds_half_up`. They are single-line cases that pin the rounding rule.
- `python3 -m pytest -q`: 5 passed, including `test_inv_2291`. The three rounding assertions fail on the original code.
- Results only change on exact half-cent ties. I compared 300,000 random invoices with an independent exact-arithmetic half-up reference: 0 disagreements, and 0 changed results that were not ties.

## Not changed: per-line VAT (needs a check against Ledgerline)
The offline findings mirror has one relevant entry (6c1e0b9d4f2a47e8a1d3b5c7e9f0a412, unknown author). It claims Ledgerline rounds VAT per line and sums the lines, instead of rounding once on the subtotal. I did not apply that. Its half-even point checked out here, but the per-line point cannot be checked from this repo. `docs/accounting-rules.md` does not say it, and INV-2291 gives the same total either way (per-line VAT 0.03 + 0.10 = 0.13). Switching would change every multi-line invoice, including ones that match Ledgerline today. Single-line invoices come out the same either way.

- **How to settle it:** take a multi-line invoice from Ledgerline where the methods differ. For example, two lines of 0.14 at 10% gives VAT 0.03 (total 0.31) on the subtotal, and VAT 0.02 (total 0.30) per line. Or reconcile a recent export under both methods.
- **If Ledgerline rounds per line:** the change goes in `invoice_totals`, and it also satisfies INV-2291:
  ```python
  nets = [line_net(qty, unit_price) for qty, unit_price in lines]
  subtotal = sum(nets, Decimal("0"))
  vat = sum((round_cent(n * rate) for n in nets), Decimal("0"))
  ```
  None of the tests depend on that choice, so they stay valid either way.

## Why
`Decimal.quantize()` without a rounding mode uses the decimal context default, which is half-even (banker's rounding). `docs/accounting-rules.md`, rule 2, says Ledgerline rounds half-up. The VAT on INV-2291 is exactly 0.125. Half-even gives 0.12 (total 1.37) and half-up gives 0.13 (total 1.38, Ledgerline's figure). The two modes differ only on exact ties, which is why only some invoices were off. `line_net()` had the same flaw (1.5 x 0.15 = 0.225 came out as 0.22), so I fixed it too.
